target_subsection: Surkhuli117, between Baghi conclusion and Kuari heading

source_claims.claim: Royal Asiatic Society transliteration; macron vowels differ from unmarked vowels in length, whereas short-marked vowels generally differ in quality. Author explicitly extends this paragraph to Jubbal,Suket,Bilaspur.
Koci/Simla aspirated sonants generally avoided; printed h after vowels often represents high falling tone rather than consonantal h. Preserve letters literally, no inferredIPA.
Surkhuli inhabitants travel through Rohru; author attributes similarity to that contact, without asserting specific lexical borrowing edges.
All genitives are adjectives and decline accordingly.
Consonant-final adjectives decline only when nominal; specified vowel-final classes have masculine oblique/plural and feminine endings. Comparison uses ku.
Most adjectives may function as adverbs and retain adjective agreement.
Beat present indicative does not change for gender; future and present conjunctive coincide with present indicative. Past agrees with object.
Negative clauses use past conditional for present indicative.

exclusion_reason: Shared phonetic exemplification not assigned to a specific named Surkhuli witness remains source-level context, not an invented lect-specific lexical attestation. Named target forms in117 and148–158 are inventoried separately.
